correctness.rationale: The centered four-level test vector has squared norm 9pq/(p+q)-4 and unit difference precisely on spoke/bridge edges, proving the universal budget bound. Equality forces zero optional rates and fixes each spoke and the bridge via vertex eigenvector equations. The four-class quotient characteristic polynomial is t(t-1)(t-3pq/N)(t-9pq/N+3) after scaling; orthogonal transverse eigenspaces have eigenvalues 3q/N and 3p/N, proving the factor-two iff criterion, both boundary cases, strictness outside by compactness, and unrestricted uniqueness inside. Exact-rational 529-pair checker passed; finite checks are corroboration not the universal argument.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary paper of Sun et al. gives the convex spectral-gap model but no explicit full equality characterization on bridge-connected dominating-hub pairs. The directly same-object barbell calculations in Boyd et al. (2007) optimize a different discrete-time SLEM criterion; Ghosh et al. (2006) optimize total effective resistance and retain nonzero internal rates. Jafarizadeh (2020), §6.3 analyzes extended barbells with a reversible discrete-time SLEM and prescribed stationary distribution, another different objective. Fiedler and Richter–Rocha cover trees, but not the stronger arbitrary-within-side supergraph rigidity and its ratio threshold. Published mathematical records matching the exact parameters did not exhibit an equivalent theorem; risks from incompletely accessible earlier full text and unindexed material remain.
residual_risks: The original 1990 tree article and the 2015 double-broom manuscript were not reliably available in full mathematical text, so known closed-form tree subcases may have been obtained previously; no novelty claim is made for those tree-only formulas.
Unindexed results or differently named absolute-algebraic-connectivity theorems for arbitrary bridged-clique supergraphs could imply the proposed statement.
The exact optimal value outside the factor-two range is not resolved; the claim there is only strict nonattainment of the stated universal upper bound.

value.rationale: This natural cost-constrained network-design class includes complete bridge barbells, all double stars, and every intermediate within-side topology; the exact sharp bound, global unique optimum, and factor-two cutoff give a structural sparsification theorem where dense intra-clique edges are optimally discarded. The boundary identifies precisely when a simple dual Rayleigh certificate is tight, while making no claim to solve the imbalanced regime. The contrast with known positive intra-clique weights for resistance minimization demonstrates why this invariant-specific conclusion is useful.
